text:
If Mikel Arteta was delighted to see the back of Eddie Howe as Newcastle’s head coach, the bad news is that another similarly awkward technical area adversary has been installed at St James’ Park.
If Arsenal’s manager never seemed to relish trips to face Howe’s old team, Arteta certainly did not enjoy this latest trip to Tyneside where Matthias Jaissle’s initially overwhelmed team fought back to earn a point courtesy of a stellar second-half performance.
At half-time the crowd had felt close to turning against Jaissle but he held his nerve and, thanks to a triple substitution and smart tactical rejig suggested that he is no mug after all.
It left Arsenal – who lost their goalkeeper David Raya to a potentially significant second-half shoulder injury – still top of the Premier League, six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City and Arteta with a face like thunder.
Only last week Bruno Guimarães claimed he was “beloved” by Newcastle fans but the club’a former captain turned Arsenal midfielder found himself serenaded by a soundtrack of boos of the sort usually reserved for Sunderland players.
Newcastle’s problem is that, despite spending an awful lot of money, they have struggled to replace last season’s now departed star trio – Guimarães, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.
That reality perhaps left Howe’s successor making a not so subtle point with his team sheet here.
Of Jaissle’s starting XI only the goalkeeper, Lukas Hornicek, the right-back Amar Dedic and the midfielder Sean Steur were signed this summer.
The other five new faces that arrived during a close season that saw a total of around £275m invested on newcomers were either benched (Nico González and Matias Fernandez-Pardo) or did not make the 20-man match day squad (Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Touré). Admittedly Ewen Jaouen is injured but, given that Bamba and Touré cost a combined £78.5m their total omission represented quite a statement. Ditto the decision to leave González and Fernandez-Pardo and their individual £50m plus price tags on the bench.
Back on the pitch the jury remained out on Hornicek. The Czech international has made some excellent saves this season but, here, his kicking proved pretty much uniformly poor and he was fortunate to be reprieved when he hesitated too long as the impressive Kai Harvertz closed in.
Jaissle’s technical frustration with his goalkeeper proved well apparent as Arsenal took increasing control of a first half that saw Newcastle’s lone striker, William Osula isolated and even their normally imperious England left back Lewis-Hall, given a thorough workout by Noni Madueke.
Much to Arteta’s chagrin, Lewis Miley, preferred to González in the midfield holding role, did his very best to slow the tempo but ultimately it proved a forlorn task. The red tide could only be stemmed for so long.
When Havertz dispossessed Hall in the wake of the latter miscontrolling a long ball, he cut inside and slid a highly intelligent, beautifully calibrated, pass across to the on-rushing Eberechi Eze. Without breaking stride, Eze exhibited perfect balance unleashed a gorgeous first-time shot that arrowed, inexorably, passed the powerless Hornicek.
As the home fans fell eerily silent, Arteta and his staff celebrated a goal sufficiently special to rebuke suggestions that his side are all about efficiency at the expense of artistry these days.
Given that on those rare moments when Newcastle’s attack looked as if it might flicker into life, Declan Rice always seemed on hand to reinforce his defence and smother any sort of danger, the omens were not bright for Jaissle.
Indeed it was a struggle to recall his side making a meaningful attacking touch inside Arsenal’s box and fans stationed near the home dugouts made their feelings plain to the manager.
Arsenal’s pressing was so good that Newcastle were left seemingly incapable of playing short passes and, instead found themselves reduced to aimless long balls. With Rice and Martin Ødegaard apparently operating on a different midfield planet an equaliser felt like a distant dream.
Yet however far fetched that vision was something Harvey Barnes would prove fully capable of buying into. The left winger is Newcastle’s best finisher. And when, early in the second half, Ødegaard made an uncharacteristic error, his heavy touch sliced the ball in Osula’s direction.
Once the Dane played it into the path of Barnes in it took a single, steadying, touch and an assured finish to leave the hitherto redundant Raya picking his shot out of the net.
Jaissle’s introduction of Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey and Anthony Elanga – who, incidentally, were all at Newcastle last season – at the expense of Dedic, Steur and Jacob Murphy at the interval was. paying dividends. Suddenly, almost astonishingly, Arsenal were the team in danger of being pressed into submission.
The home side had begun closing their guests down far higher up the pitch and, along the way had morphed into an infinitely more menacing team.
Soon, they were ahead in the wake of a Hall corner headed down by Dan Burn, allowing Malick Thiaw to stab the ball beyond Raya.
Shortly afterwards Arsenal’s goalkeeper was helped off the pitch in evident pain after sustaining a nasty looking left shoulder injury during an ostensibly benign collision with Osula. On came Kepa Arrizabalaga in a triple substitution also featuring the withdrawl of Guimarães.
Madueke though was still around and he reminded everyone of his presence by meeting the counter-attacking Ødegaard’s stellar pass, dummying a couple of defenders and watching his slightly deflected shot evade Hornicek’s grasp.
digest_he:
משחק דרמטי הסתיים בתיקו לאחר שניוקאסל התאוששה מפיגור והצליחה לכפות חלוקת נקודות מול ארסנל המוליכה. המחצית הראשונה הייתה בשליטת התותחנים, כאשר קאי האברץ בישל באמנות לאברצ'י אזה שכבש שער יפהפה והעניק יתרון לאורחים.

אולם, במחצית השנייה חל מהפך במשחק הודות לחילופי טקטיקה ושינויים שביצע המאמן של ניוקאסל. הארווי בארנס השווה את התוצאה לאחר ניצול טעות בהגנה, ולאחר מכן מאליק תיה והפך את התוצאה עבור המארחים בנגיחה מדויקת מקרן.

המצב החמיר עבור ארסנל כאשר השוער דויד ראיה נפצע בכתפו ונאלץ לרדת מהמגרש כשהוא סובל מכאבים עזים, והוחלף על ידי קפה אריסבלאגה. למרות זאת, נוני מדואקה הצליח להציל נקודה יקרה עבור ארסנל בדקות הסיום לאחר שקיבל מסירה מדויקת והבקיע את השוויון.
